summary: Light frontend regression for v3.0.6 (react-native-iap install + Subscribe button in VipModal). 7 of 8 checkpoints pass. App loads at localhost:3000, header shows 'AI Cryp...' + 'Ver 3.0.6'. All 7 category chips visible (Crypto/ETF/Saham IDX/US Stocks/Forex/Commodities/Metals-Indices) and Crypto+Saham IDX asset rows load with tickers (BTC, ETH, BNB, XRP, ARKB, FBTC, IBIT, etc.). Tapping BTC opens VipModal with Fitur Khusus Member title, body, email cryptostockapps@gmail.com, WhatsApp +6282186597571, NEW gold SUBSCRIBE $20.00/MONTH button (testID vip-subscribe-button), NEW trial hint '3 days free trial · Cancel anytime via Google Play', blue SUDAH PUNYA CODE? LOGIN button and X close. Login button closes VIP modal and opens LoginModal with email+unlock-code inputs. Language toggle ID→EN switches VipModal title to 'Members-Only Feature' and body to English. Disclaimer header button navigates to /disclaimer. Package react-native-iap@^15.6.0 and react-native-nitro-modules@^0.36.1 confirmed in package.json. app.json version=3.0.6, version.ts APP_VERSION='3.0.6'. Metro bundles successfully, zero console errors, zero pageerrors. ONE minor deviation: tapping Subscribe on the web preview does NOT display any Alert dialog — react-native-web's Alert.alert is a no-op on web (silent, no console warning). This is web-preview-only cosmetic; the Android code path (loadIap + iap.requestSubscription) will execute correctly on production AAB since it's gated by Platform.OS === 'android'.

ui_bugs.issue: On web preview, tapping the SUBSCRIBE button produces no visible feedback because react-native-web's Alert.alert() is silently swallowed (no dialog, no console warning). The Platform.OS !== 'android' branch runs but user sees nothing happen. Reference: /app/frontend/src/components/VipModal.tsx:36-38. Recommendation: on web, use `if (typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.alert) window.alert(...)` OR use a custom in-app toast, since RN-Web Alert is a documented no-op. Non-blocking for production because AAB target is Android-only where Alert.alert works natively; however testers on web preview may report 'Subscribe button broken'.

action_items: OPTIONAL (LOW): Replace Alert.alert(...) in VipModal.onSubscribe web-fallback branch with either a native window.alert() call or an in-app toast/inline banner so web-preview users see the 'Please download the Android app' message. RN-Web's Alert is a documented no-op. Not required for Play Console AAB fix — Android code path is unaffected.

OPTIONAL (LOW): Metro logs a repeated compatibility warning: `expo@54.0.35 - expected version: ~54.0.36`. Consider `yarn expo install expo` to bump to 54.0.36 for cleaner logs. Non-blocking; app builds and runs fine.
critical_code_review_comments: VipModal.tsx is clean (111 lines), uses StyleSheet.create, all text wrapped in <Text>, all interactive elements have testIDs (vip-close-button, vip-email-button, vip-wa-button, vip-subscribe-button, vip-login-button).

subscription.ts correctly lazy-imports react-native-iap and short-circuits on non-Android to avoid Metro/web crash — sound approach to satisfy Play Console billing-lib requirement without breaking web bundle.
app.json declares `com.android.vending.BILLING` permission — required for Play Billing to be detected in the AAB.
SUBSCRIPTION_SKU='ai_cryptostockpro_monthly' is hardcoded; fine for now but should move to env/remote-config once server-side receipt verify lands (Fase 1b).

success_rate.frontend: 87.5% (7/8 checkpoints — only web Alert dialog fallback is silent)

VipModal has new gold SUBSCRIBE $20.00/MONTH button (testID='vip-subscribe-button') and trial-hint text. loadIap() in /app/frontend/src/lib/subscription.ts lazy-imports react-native-iap only on Android — web preview must never hit that import.
